subject: Private GPU fleet rightsizing: steady throughput targets, admission-control knobs, and graceful-deg runbook
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Joe Ellis <joe.ellis@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private fleet sizing kickoff — baseline, steady-state vs bursts

Hi team,

Opening thread for the ACME private deployment sizing work. Joe from ACME joined our sync last week and shared a coarse traffic snapshot — attached is a CSV export (acme-load-profile.csv). High-level asks from ACME:

- Sustained conversational throughput target: 1250 tokens/s across the private pool (95th percentile)
- Peak bursts: up to ~7x sustained for 3–10s, typical at business-hour start/stop windows
- Hard SLA: 99.5% requests < 300ms LL (inference-only p50/p95 targets to be defined)

Goals for this email: align on headroom/safety factors, admission control policy, and a short list of kernel/network knobs we should test during the POC.

Concrete questions:
1) What steady-state capacity (GPUs) should we size for given 1250 tokens/s sustained, assuming we use the 70B fp16 model variant ACME requested?
2) How much headroom for warm burst absorption vs cold-warm (KV cache) warmup? Recommend an overprovision factor or queued-admission approach?
3) Any immediate NIC/OS tuning (RPS, ephemeral ports, TCP backlog, irqbalance, SR-IOV) that should be in the runbook?

Please reply with estimates and a sketch of the admission-control rules (token/s or request/s throttles, queue depth, fallback variants). I want to have a concise runbook draft we can share with ACME by EOD Tuesday.

Attachments: acme-load-profile.csv (sample 72hr export)

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Joe Ellis <joe.ellis@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet sizing kickoff — baseline, steady-state vs bursts

Thanks Marissa,

Quick initial thoughts after a preliminary run on our local perf model (see attached throughput-model.xlsx):

1) Baseline math (assumptions)
   - Model: 70B fp16 optimized path, KV-cache hit for steady chats (typical prefix lengths 200 tokens)
   - Observed median token/s per A100-80GB (optimized runtime, batching 8–16): ~85–95 tokens/s sustained (p50) for generation workload. p95 is ~70 tokens/s under realistic concurrency mix.
   - Network overhead (TLS + JSON payloads) ~5–8% added latency, negligible for throughput math but matters for tails.

2) Steady-state recommendation
   - To hit 1250 tokens/s 95th, use conservative token-per-GPU = 65 tokens/s (p95-focused). -> ~20 GPUs (1250/65 = 19.2)
   - Add a 25% steady headroom for maintenance & node rotation -> plan for 25 GPUs in the pool. This accounts for planned capacity and small unexpected spikes without immediate autoscale.

3) Burst handling / admission control
   - Do NOT try to absorb 7x bursts purely by overprovisioning. 7x sustained would be ~8k tokens/s and is cost-prohibitive.
   - Strategy: admission-control + short-term soft-failover to smaller but cheaper model variant (35B int8) + queueing.
   - Admission rules: token-based token_burst_bucket with refill rate = steady allocation (1250 t/s) and max_burst = 5 * steady for 6s (configurable). When bucket exhausted, apply one of: 1) queued requests with TTL 8s and progressive backoff, 2) downgrade path to 35B int8 for best-effort, 3) reject with graceful 429 + Retry-After header.

4) KV-cache warmup / cold starts
   - KV warmup penalty: first full-context request to a warmed session ~1.0x baseline; cold context can be 1.6–2.2x more expensive depending on cache policies. Recommend sticky routing (session pinning) + proactive cache-warm probe (on user login) during ramp windows.

5) Network / OS knobs to include in runbook (short list)
   - NIC: enable RSS, disable GRO/LRO for TCP batches if low-latency traffic; tune tx/rx ring sizes to 4096 where supported.
   - Kernel: net.core.somaxconn=4096, tcp_max_syn_backlog=2048, net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1, net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=1024 65535.
   - Keepalive and TLS session resumption enabled; reuse TLS sessions where possible to reduce handshake cost.

6) Observability gates (what to monitor during POC)
   - per-GPU token/s, per-request tail latency (p50/p95/p99), KV cache hit ratio, admission-control drop rate, queue depth, OS runqueue length, netdev drops.

I'll push the spreadsheet with perf runs to the shared drive and follow up with a workload-specific sizing script (we can iterate on the tokens/GPU assumption).

Attachments: throughput-model.xlsx

--Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private fleet sizing kickoff — baseline, steady-state vs bursts

Thanks Dev — good numbers and conservative safety margins. A couple of operational decisions to propose:

- Commitment: We plan to offer ACME a committed pool of 25 GPUs (A100-80GB class) for the initial quarter with an autoscale headroom policy up to +40% via burst credits and partner-managed overflow. This matches the 25 GPUs you recommended and leaves room for maintenance windows.

- Canary + rollout policy: We'll do a staged rollout: 10 GPUs first (functional + perf validation), then expand to 18, then 25 after 48h of stable metrics. Canary should use 35B variant as fallback route for degraded quality.

- Admission control defaults: implement Dev's token_bucket scheme with a conservative max_burst=4x for first pass. TTL for queued requests = 8s as suggested. Expose the config via the Redwood Console (per-route override) so ACME can tune.

- Networking ops: loop in CloudPartner SRE (cc'd) to validate SR-IOV vs VPC passthrough. Tessa, can you schedule the network validation call for Friday with CP SRE and ACME ops?

Action items:
1) Dev: produce a short test matrix for the canary (latency targets, KV-warm vs cold, 35B fallback quality check) — due Tue EOD.
2) Tessa: schedule network call + attach ACL/peering checklist — due Thu.
3) Marissa: draft runbook for ACME that includes admission-control, monitoring gates, escalation path — due Tue EOD.

If no objections, I'll convert the above into a short SoW bullet we can attach to the draft.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Solutions

Subject: Re: Private fleet sizing kickoff — baseline, steady-state vs bursts

Thanks all — this looks sensible. A few clarifications from ACME infra: 

- The 7x bursts are real but typically last 4–6s and happen ~3x/day at regional roll times. We are OK with queued retries if the user is notified. Prioritize p95 latency and a smooth degradation path over strict absolute throughput during short bursts.

- We can accept the 35B int8 fallback for quality under severe load, but we need a per-route toggle and audit logging for any downgraded responses (for later analysis).

- Shared doc: I added a traffic-sample annotation to the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cACME-traffic-spec) with example sessions. Please reference it for KV warmup probe placement.

I'll keep ops@acme.com available for the network call Friday.

—Joe

Subject: Private fleet rightsizing — consolidated runbook draft (for ACME review)

Team — attaching the first draft of the runbook (private-fleet-rightsizing-runbook-draft.md) and a short checklist below. This captures decisions and the immediate POC plan.

Summary / decisions:
- Committed pool: 25 A100-80GB GPUs (steady target using conservative 65 tokens/s p95 assumption).
- Canary rollout: 10 -> 18 -> 25 (48h stable windows).
- Admission control: token bucket refill=1250 t/s, initial max_burst=4x for canary; fallback to 35B int8 when queue TTL exceeded or when bucket exhausted; respond 429 + Retry-After for requests that exceed queued TTL.
- KV-cache: enable session pinning, add a warm-probe on session start, instrument warm vs cold cost in metrics.
- Networking: SR-IOV preferred if partner provides, otherwise tune NIC rings and kernel TCP knobs (see Dev's list).
- Observability: per-GPU tokens/s, cache hit ratio, queue depth, drop/reject rate, p95/p99, and an automated alert if admission-drop-rate > 1% for > 10min.

Short checklist for POC:
- Perf team: run the 72hr steady + burst emulation using throughput-model.xlsx scenarios (Dev).
- Net/Partner SRE: validate SR-IOV and ring size changes in staging; confirm egress rules and cryptographic offload (CP SRE).
- Solutions: prepare SoW bullets re: committed pool and overflow policy (Laura).
- ACME: confirm whether session pinning is allowed in their client and confirm which user flows need strict latency vs degraded-mode acceptance (Joe/ops).

Next steps: I'll share the markdown runbook with ACME via the Drive link and convert the checklist into a short SoW. We'll use the Friday network call to lock down SR-IOV vs passthrough.

Attachments: private-fleet-rightsizing-runbook-draft.md

Thanks all —
Marissa
